title: guyaclim
text:
Introduction
The general idea is to test the development of a clean and automated database of consolidated raw microclimate data from microsensors (TOMOST, HOBO, …) in French Guiana.

title: guyaclim
text:
Usage
guyaclim database building and analyses rely on the quarto documents *.qmd that can be run with R and associated environment defined with renv.

title: guyaclim
text:
Project
guyaclim includes:

Analyse of the data with associated documentation and figures:

Reproductive analyses in index``.qmd
Resulting page in index.html

All raw data from the database in data/
All datasets in datasets/
The consolidated database in db/
The R scripts in scripts/
R environment definition with renv in renv/ and renv/lock
R files (.Rbuildignore , .Rdata , .Rprofile , .Rhistory)
Git and GitHub files (.gitignore)
Project documentation (README.qmd , README.md , NEWS.md , LICENSE)

title: Raw data
text: All raw data directly taken from the field are gathered in the data/ folder. The following pages describes raw data structure, metadata and associated content, and how we are consolidating first by site x project x sensor and then in a single global database.

title: Structure
text:
The raw database is structured with a main data/ folder in which we find a combination of each site (e.g. Paracou/) each project (e.g. ALT/) and each sensors (e.g TOMST) in each folder (e.g. Paracou_TOMST_ALT/). All levels are documented through READMEs. Sites, project, and sensors are separately described below.


Code
fs::dir_tree("data", recurse = 0, type = "directory")

├── Laussat_HESS_TOMST
├── NouraguesPP_ALT_TOMST
├── Paracou_ALT_HOBO

In each site-project-sensor folders we find a folder by data collection campaign with its date (e.g. 20240920/) and associated sensors metadata (metadata.xlsx/) and campaigns metadata (e.g. 20240920.xlsx). Available campaigns are described in campaigns.xlsx/ . Other information specific to a folder can also be included and will be described in corresponding page.

title: Metadata
text:
Sensors metadata
Sensors metadata are project specific but they should include sensor serial number (e.g. TomstSensorNum here) and corresponding study ID (e.g. TomstID) for associated information. An ID can have in this case several sensors associated as the change of sensors here. The metadata may contain associated ecological data (e.g. light, habitat, edge) and geolocation data (e.g. distance to 3 nearest neighbours here). They should be described in a metadata sheet, in the README, or in the corresponding html file. Metadata should also include the project or acquisition beginning and end, and eventually calibration dates.

title: Data processing
text:
Sensor data reading
Data processing is for the moment pretty basic based on R scripts in scripts:
First each sensor (by model and not brand, not the case yet) will have a reading function to read the specific data file (e.g. data.csv for TOMST and data.xlsx for HOBO). This is the read_{sensor}_data.R function.

title: Data processing
text:
Sensor campaign reading
Then a function ease the reading for a whole campaign (sampling date) called read_{sensor}_campaign.R . This is sensor specific as metadata should be sensor specific (and maybe project specific?).

title: Data processing
text:
Sensor project reading
Finally, a function ease the assembly at the whole sensor x project level and is generic with a switch depending on the sensor. This is read_{sensor}_project.R .

title: Data processing
text:
To do


Column names need harmonization.
We need data check functions.
An automatic reports could be produced for errors (discussed at which level). I think the best would be at the sensor-project level with maybe a snakemake and singularity worklow or a simple R workflow to automate it with outputs in a separate place and thus sensor project databases and a single common databases (maybe sqlight for big ones).
Reading functions will depend on the sensors and will need to be made generic on the way they open and handle data.
We need to had soil data or parameters for soil moisture.
Date filtering should be used the earliest to save memory.

title: Datasets processing
text:
Datasets processing is for the moment pretty basic based on the following chunk:


Code
paracou_alt_tomst <- read_tsv("datasets/Paracou_ALT_TOMST.tsv") |> 
  mutate(site = "Paracou", project = "ALT", sensor = "TOMST") |> 
  select(site, project, sensor, id, sensornum, date,
         t_soil, t_surface, t_air, moisture) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = t_soil:moisture, names_to = "variable")
nouraguespp_alt_tomst <- read_tsv("datasets/NouraguesPP_ALT_TOMST.tsv") |> 
  mutate(site = "NouraguesPP", project = "ALT", sensor = "TOMST") |> 
  select(site, project, sensor, id, sensornum, date,
         t_soil, t_surface, t_air, moisture) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = t_soil:moisture, names_to = "variable")
arbocel_hest_tomst <- read_tsv("datasets/Arbocel_HES_TOMST.tsv") |> 
  mutate(site = "Arbocel", project = "HES", sensor = "TOMST") |> 
  select(site, project, sensor, id, sensornum, date,
         t_soil, t_surface, t_air, moisture) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = t_soil:moisture, names_to = "variable")
bind_rows(
  paracou_alt_tomst,
  arbocel_hest_tomst,
  nouraguespp_alt_tomst
) |> 
  write_tsv("db/guyaclim.tsv")


It combines all datasets across sites, sensor and projects in a single database (csv or sqlite or both). But to do so some metadata will be lost on the way. Current columns are:

site - site name
project - project name
sensor - sensor name
id - sensor id in the project
sensornum - manufacturer sensor id
date - sampling date and time
variable - variable measured:

t_soil: soil temperature (-8 cm for TOMST)
t_air: air temperature (15 cm for TOMST)
t_surface: surface temperature (0 cm for TOMST)
moisture: electric moisture to be transformed into soil water content with soil texture (table to be added)

value - value of the measured variable

t_soil: soil temperature in degree Celsisus
t_air: air temperature in degree Celsisus
t_surface: surface temperature in degree Celsisus
moisture: electric moisture

  group_by(site, project, sensor, id, variable) |> 
  summarise(n = n()) |> 
  group_by(site, project, sensor, variable) |> 
  summarise(min = min(n), median = median(n), max = max(n)) |>
